To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the primary CWR22 prostate cancer xenograft has aneuploid karyotype, whereas all of the CWR22‐relapsed tumors are hyperdiploid, and that the relapsed tumors have a greater number of chromosomal abnormalities than does the primary CWR‐22 tumor.

the CWR22 xenograft is a human prostatic carcinoma that has a near‐normal male karyotype with a 1q gain, and that the relapsed xenografts have a similar near‐normal karyotype, but with additional chromosome changes.

the primary tumor (CWR22), and four relapsed tumor lines (CWR22‐R1, CWR22‐P1, CWR‐P2, CWR‐R3), have similar karyotypes, with the most frequent chromosome aberrations being 1p, 3, 6q, 9p and 10q deletions and trisomy 7 and 8.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization and molecular cytogenetic studies on CWR22 and its relapsed tumors.
the cytogenetic and molecular analysis of a serially transplantable prostatic carcinoma xenograph, CWR22.
the cytogenetic and genetic characterization of the CWR22 and its relapsed tumors, CWR22‐1 through CWR22‐4, and the establishment of cell lines from these tumors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CWR22 and the CWR22‐relapsed xenografts are genetically heterogeneous.
the CWR22 and the four CWR22‐relapsed strains are not identical to each other.

CWR22 and the CWR22‐derived xenografts are not representative of the majority of prostate cancers, and that they have a relatively small number of cytogenetic alterations, with no consistent abnormalities that could be used for prognostication or as a target for therapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CWR22 is a near‐diploid cell line, and that the karyotype of CWR22‐relapsed xenografts was more complex and varied with each relapsed tumor.
there are no consistent cytogenetic changes between the primary CWR22 and the relapsed xenografts.
the karyotypes of the CWR22 and four CWR22‐ R tumors were similar to one another and to each other.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CWR22 and the four relapsed xenografts have different cytogenetic profiles.
the CWR22‐derived xenografts have a remarkably consistent karyotype.
CWR22 and its relapsed strains are cytogenetically stable, and the relapses are not due to chromosomal changes.
